question: Three numbers are in the ratio of 3 ∶ 4 ∶ 5 respectively and their LCM is 2,400. Their H.C.F. is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Since the given ratio parts 3, 4, and 5 are co-prime, their LCM is simply their product: 3 × 4 × 5 = 60.

The total LCM of the numbers is equal to their H.C.F multiplied by the LCM of their ratios.

⇒ Total LCM = H.C.F × (LCM of ratios)

⇒ 2400 = H.C.F × 60

⇒ H.C.F = 2400 ÷ 60 = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Ratio of the three numbers = 3 : 4 : 5

LCM of the three numbers = 2400

**Formula Used:**

If numbers are in the ratio a : b : c, then the numbers can be written as ax, bx, and cx, where x is their highest common factor (H.C.F).

The LCM of ax, bx, and cx is given by x × LCM(a, b, c).

 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• 
• H.C.F = x 1st = 3x 2nd = 4x 3rd = 5x LCM = 60x = 2400 x = 40 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the three numbers be 3x, 4x, and 5x, where x is their H.C.F.

⇒ The LCM of the ratio parts 3, 4, and 5 is 60.

⇒ Hence, the LCM of the three numbers 3x, 4x, and 5x is 60x.

⇒ It is given that the total LCM is 2400.

⇒ 60x = 2400

⇒ x = 2400 ÷ 60

⇒ x = 40

⇒ Therefore, the H.C.F of the given numbers is 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relation between H.C.F and LCM (For two numbers)

For any two numbers 'a' and 'b', the product of the numbers is equal to the product of their H.C.F and LCM (a × b = H.C.F × LCM). Note that this general formula is exclusively applicable to two numbers only.

Co-prime Numbers

Two or more numbers are called co-prime if their H.C.F is 1. When numbers are reduced to their simplest ratio form, the individual ratio parts become co-prime to each other.

H.C.F and LCM of Fractions

H.C.F of fractions = (H.C.F of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).

LCM of fractions = (LCM of numerators) ÷ (H.C.F of denominators).
